samples.summary: Border clear can now DELETE a spill ghost cell whose value is the empty string, dropping its `spillAnchor` marker
samples.evidence: `applyBorderPatch` ends with `const newCell = compactCell(cell, style); if (isEmptyCell(newCell)) { await this.store.delete(anchor); return; }` (sheet.ts:4152-4156). `isEmptyCell` (style-mutation.ts:48-52) treats `v === ''` as no content and ignores the spill fields entirely, so a spill ghost written by the calculator as `{ v: '', spillAnchor: 'A1' }` (calculator.ts:141 — `v: values[dr]?.[dc] ?? ''`, i.e. any blank element of a spilled array) that carries a border style is DELETED when the user clears borders. Under the old `setStyle` path this could not happen for a border preset, because `setStyle` persisted `bt/bl/br/bb: false` and the cell therefore always kept a non-empty `s`; pruning to `undefined` is what newly reaches the delete branch. Losing the ghost marker removes the cell from the anchor's ghost set: the calculator's cleanup (`ghostCell?.spillAnchor === sref`, calculator.ts:80) no longer recognises it, and if the user later types into that now-plain cell the spill becomes blocked and the anchor renders `#REF!` where previously the cell was protected read-only ghost territory. This directly contradicts the comment added in this diff (sheet.ts:4112-4114 and style-mutation.ts:57-60) claiming the rewrite "cannot orphan a spill range" — that only holds on the `store.set` branch, not the `store.delete` branch. The new spill test only uses a ghost with `v: '0'` (formatting.test.ts, `should keep spill metadata across a border apply and clear`), so the empty-value ghost is untested. Note `clearCellStylesInRange` (sheet.ts:2047-2052) has the same shape, so the underlying `isEmptyCell`/spill blind spot is pre-existing; this change adds a second reachable path to it.

samples.summary: Conflict check can keep an unnecessary `false` when the conflicting range-style patch is itself overridden by a later patch
samples.evidence: `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys` -> `hasConflictingStyleSourceForKey` (style-mutation.ts:253-266) scans `sources.rangeStyles` and returns true on ANY intersecting patch whose value differs from the target, without regard for a later patch in the list that supersedes it. So if patch[0] sets `bt: true` over A1 and patch[1] sets `bt: false` over A1, a `clear` preset on A1 still writes `bt: false` onto the cell even though nothing would be inherited — the exact residue this change set out to remove. Conservative rather than dangerous (the rendered result is correct), and identical to the behaviour of the existing `addRangeStylePatch` path, so this is a residual gap in the fix's stated goal rather than a wrong pixel.

verdict.reason: The finding checks out in full. applyBorderPatch's terminal delete branch (sheet.ts:4152-4156) uses isEmptyCell, which (style-mutation.ts:48-52 via hasCellContent at 38-42) treats v==='' as contentless and ignores the spill fields entirely, so a ghost cell of the form { v: '', spillAnchor } — exactly what calculator.ts:141 writes for any blank element of a spilled array, persisted verbatim by Sheet.setCell (sheet.ts:937-939) — is DELETED when a border style is applied and then cleared. The path is reachable and unguarded: setRangeBorders (sheet.ts:4064-4088) only checks selection type and a cell cap, collectBorderTargets (sheet.ts:4160+) excludes no spill cells, and with the border keys pruned to undefined the early returns at sheet.ts:4145-4150 do not fire because prev (the previously applied border style) is truthy. Losing the marker breaks two invariants that read it: the ghost read-only guard `if (existing?.spillAnchor) return;` (sheet.ts:1041) and the calculator's ownership check `ghostCell?.spillAnchor === sref` (calculator.ts:80); subsequent user input in that now-plain cell satisfies the blocker predicate at calculator.ts:109 and forces the anchor to #REF! (calculator.ts:118-126). The comments claiming the rewrite "cannot orphan a spill range" (sheet.ts:4112-4114, style-mutation.ts:57-60) hold only for the store.set branch. The new test (formatting.test.ts:418-450) uses v: '0', so the empty-value ghost is untested. Real, reachable broken-invariant/data-loss bug in the correctness lane; no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: applyBorderPatch writes cells through compactCell, which silently drops spill metadata (spillAnchor/spillRows/spillCols/spillBlocked)
finding.evidence: `const newCell = compactCell(cell, style)` (sheet.ts:4029). `compactCell` (style-mutation.ts:53-65) copies ONLY `v`, `f` and `s`; `Cell` also carries `spillRows`, `spillCols`, `spillAnchor`, `spillBlocked` (model/core/types.ts:209-217), and YorkieStore.normalizeCell (frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:228-239) does persist them, so the loss is caused here. `collectBorderTargets` (sheet.ts:4043-4056) enumerates every cell in the selection with no read-only skip — contrast toggleCheckboxesInRange, which explicitly skips `cell?.f || cell?.spillAnchor` (sheet.ts:3906). Consequences of applying e.g. 'all borders' over a spilled array: (a) a ghost cell loses `spillAnchor`, so the next recalculation treats it as user data and blocks the spill with #REF! (calculator.ts:109-125); (b) the spill anchor loses `spillRows`/`spillCols`, so setData's ghost-cleanup contract (sheet.ts:1003-1008) never fires and stale ghosts are orphaned. The same defect exists in `setStyle` (sheet.ts:3679), so it is pre-existing behavior — but this change re-implements the write inline and is the border path's new write site, and the cheap fix (`{...cell}` spread instead of compactCell, or skipping ghost/anchor cells) belongs here.

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise is factually absent from this repository. It claims `compactCell` copies only `v`, `f` and `s`, thereby dropping spill metadata. The actual sole definition at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/style-mutation.ts:62-86 explicitly copies `spillRows` (70-72), `spillCols` (73-75), `spillAnchor` (76-78) and `spillBlocked` (79-81) before attaching the style, and its doc comment (55-61) states this exists specifically so a style-only write such as a border preset cannot orphan a spill range. `applyBorderPatch` (sheet.ts:4152) passes the full stored cell (read at 4132) into that function, so the ghost retains `spillAnchor` and the anchor retains `spillRows`/`spillCols`. A repo-wide grep for `compactCell` over `**/*.ts` finds exactly one definition and sheet.ts:127-139 imports that one, so no shadowing variant exists. packages/sheets/test/model/style-mutation.test.ts:13-34 asserts anchor, ghost and blocked spill fields survive a style rewrite. Both claimed consequences (#REF! on recalculation from a lost `spillAnchor`; orphaned ghosts from lost `spillRows`/`spillCols`) depend on a drop that does not happen, and the same disposes of the aside about `setStyle` (sheet.ts:3722), which uses the same spill-preserving helper. The only accurate observation — that `collectBorderTargets` (sheet.ts:4160-4182) has no read-only skip — is harmless once spill metadata is preserved, since bordering a ghost or anchor is then a benign style-only write with no data loss.
